summary: An idle interrupt cancels a pending MCP startup but never schedules reconnection, so the server tools disappear from later turns.
scenario: A configured streamable HTTP MCP server has entered initialize; an idle Op::Interrupt cancels it; the server then becomes responsive; the next unchanged-settings turn makes no second initialize request and omits the server tool from the model request.

evidence.point: Idle interrupt calls cancel_mcp_startup after abort_all_tasks.
The interrupt does not invalidate McpRefresh; unchanged auth, environments, and capability roots leave the canceled runtime published for the next turn.
Cancellation becomes a shared startup result; reconnect_failed_startup only handles Failed, not Cancelled.
Binding capture omits a server whose completed client result is an error.

trace: Op::Interrupt -> Session::interrupt_task -> cancel_mcp_startup -> McpRuntime::cancel_startup -> McpServerConnection::cancel_startup -> CancellationToken; next turn -> mcp_runtime_for_step -> refresh_mcp_if_dirty returns with no pending refresh -> published AsyncManagedClient returns cached Cancelled -> capture_binding_with_metadata omits server tool -> model request has no namespace.

authority.quote: After a transient startup cancellation, a later turn must be able to use a now-ready configured MCP server without requiring an unrelated configuration change.

proof.name: interrupted_idle_mcp_startup_reconnects_for_next_turn
proof.output: Compiled and ran on unchanged production; two attempts failed with actual (initialize_attempts, tool_advertised) = (1, false), expected (2, true). Raw log: red-test-final.log.

severity: High user impact within the affected session: a common idle interrupt during slow server startup permanently removes that server's tools until an explicit refresh or another unrelated reprojection; no data loss was shown.

summary: An idle startup interrupt does not cancel an already ready client.
checked: McpServerConnection::cancel_startup checks startup_complete before canceling its token; the existing ready-client test covers continued tool catalog access.
reopens_if: A ready client can have startup_complete false or a different interrupt path cancels its transport.

summary: Canceling a claimed dirty refresh before publication does not lose its invalidation marker.
checked: The refresh guard restores pending on Drop unless publication completed, while the publication gate waits until current.store before releasing startup notifications.
reopens_if: A refresh path bypasses the guard or new side effects occur before current.store.
